tool_input.content:
# Issue 5: Chainsaw rule

## Outcome

Only members who did the induction for the chainsaw's safety class (class C) can borrow it.
Other members are told why they cannot.

## Requirements

- When a member without the "C" induction asks to borrow a class C item, the system shall refuse and give a reason that names the induction.
- Where a member has the "C" induction, the system shall let them borrow a free class C item.
- When a member holds only other inductions, such as "B", the system shall still refuse a class C item.
- While an item is class A or class B, the system shall decide as before, without needing an induction.
- If a class C item is in repair or already out, the system shall refuse it even when the member has the "C" induction.

## Must not change

- Anything under `src/auth/`.
- The refusal for a tool in repair or already out, and its reasons.
- The existing tests.
- Money stays in integer cents.

## Out of scope

- Recording or granting inductions.
- Rules for class B tools.
- Changes to the desk screens or the server routes.

## Done when

- The new tests in `tests/items/borrow.test.ts` pass.
- `bun run gate` exits 0.

# Plan for issue 5: Chainsaw rule

## Files to change

- `src/items/borrow.ts`: the only file. `canBorrow` already receives the member but does not read
  it. Add the induction rule here, and remove the now-false "member is not read yet" comment and
  the `biome-ignore` for the unused parameter.

No other file needs a change. `src/desk.ts` and `src/server.ts` already call `canBorrow` with a
member built by `toMember` in `src/db.ts`, which splits the stored text ("B,C") into a list.
Not touched: `src/auth/`, any test file, the desk screens, the server routes.

## Steps

1. Keep the repair check first, then the out check, exactly as they are (same reasons).
2. After those, if `item.safety_class === "C"` and `member.inductions` does not include `"C"`,
   return `{ ok: false, reason }`.
3. Make the reason name the induction and the tool, e.g. `` `${item.name} needs the C induction` ``
   (the test lowercases it and looks for "induction").
4. Otherwise return `{ ok: true }`; class A and B never reach the induction check's refusal.
5. Remove the stale comment and the `biome-ignore` line, and keep the function under 40 lines.

## Risks

- Safety: a wrong order or a loose match could hand out the chainsaw. The check is an exact
  match on `"C"` in the list, so a member with only "B" is refused, and an empty list is refused.
  Repair and out checks stay ahead of the induction check, so an inducted member still cannot
  take a tool in repair or already out.
- Safety: the stored induction text could have spaces or lower case. `toMember` only splits on
  commas, so compare exactly and treat anything else as not inducted (fail closed). Do not edit
  `toMember` in this change.
- Member privacy: the reason names only the item and the induction needed. It must not include
  the member's name, contact details or their list of inductions.
- Money: nothing here touches amounts or the deposit; `deposit_cents` stays integer cents and
  unread.
- Regression: class A and B tools must decide as before. No new rule applies to them.

## How to check

- `bun test tests/items` passes, including these in `tests/items/borrow.test.ts`:
  - a member without the C induction cannot take a class C tool (reason mentions "induction")
  - a member with the C induction can take a free class C tool
  - a member with only the B induction cannot take a class C tool
  - a class B tool needs no induction
  - an inducted member cannot take a class C tool that is in repair or out
  - the existing class A and repair tests still pass
- `bun run gate` exits 0 with every test passing, and `.factory/gate.json` records the pass.
- `git diff` shows changes only in `src/items/borrow.ts` (and no `src/auth/` or test file).
